key_insight: OMatG-FC generates inorganic crystals by learning atomic species and cell volume within fixed structural frameworks, achieving a reported state-of-the-art stable, unique, and novel (S.U.N.) rate below the convex hull.
engineering_relevance: Conditioning on known crystal frameworks reduces generation dimensionality and offers a targeted route to materials discovery without learning atomic packings from scratch.
method: Fix fractional atomic coordinates and unit-volume lattice vectors.
Learn atomic species using discrete flow matching and cell-volume scaling using stochastic interpolants.
Generate candidate materials that can include unseen, stable prototypes derived from known frameworks.
evidence_signal: The authors analyze duplicate frameworks in MP-20, provide a framework-based split, and report LeMat-GenBench evaluation using three ML interatomic potentials.
watch_item: Fixed-framework conditioning restricts exploration of new atomic packings, and ML-predicted stability does not establish experimental synthesizability.
